page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core of an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 7.0 GB of system memory, equating to 3.5 GB per core. The CPU allocation is dedicated, with hyper-threading enabled (2 threads per core). Cache specifications include 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals highly polarized performance characteristics. The instance excels in single-core operations, achieving top-tier (top 10%) results in stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core testing. Conversely, multi-core and multi-threaded benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores, fall into the weak category (bottom 25%). Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is average, while small cached block read-only bandwidth is weak. Cryptographic and database operations also rank in the bottom 25%.

Given its dedicated hardware profile and low resource density, the c4d-standard-2 offers a qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for workloads that are strictly single-threaded or require high single-core throughput without demanding massive memory capacity. It is not suitable for parallelized computing, large-scale database operations, or memory-intensive tasks due to its 7.0 GB memory limit and weak multi-core scaling. Appropriate workloads include lightweight single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and low-concurrency web serving.
